title: Site Selection for Retail & Logistics

blueprintSignals.name: Catchment population
blueprintSignals.definition: residents within a 15-minute drive weighted by purchasing power
blueprintSignals.asOfRule: Census data age, so adjust with recent growth

blueprintSignals.name: Competitor density
blueprintSignals.definition: number and size of competing stores within the catchment
blueprintSignals.asOfRule: Definitions of a competitor differ, so use a consistent category

blueprintSignals.name: Mobility flows
blueprintSignals.definition: anonymised footfall or vehicle counts passing the site, per hour
blueprintSignals.asOfRule: Panels are samples, so check representativeness

blueprintSignals.name: Network fit
blueprintSignals.definition: average distance from the site to the company's hubs and suppliers
blueprintSignals.asOfRule: Road conditions change, so use time and not distance

engineFeatures.meaning: the strongest continuous driver; interacts with x2 and shifts in the last quarter
modifies the effect of x1 and sets the noise level
a smooth non-linear effect that a straight line cannot fit
a categorical segment with its own level and noise

label: For "Site Selection for Retail & Logistics": Rank candidate locations for a store or warehouse by expected revenue or cost, using demographics, mobility, competition and network fit. Define the label exactly as in milestone M1: what counts as a positive or a correct outcome, and when it becomes known. Design around this trap first: Survivor sites are those that were opened and kept, so failed locations are missing from the data.
